issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method signature is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement and the template Main expect a no-argument method messageOnRide():String, but the solution defines Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) and implements it with an int parameter in Pig and Seal. This parameter mismatch will confuse students (the provided example Main calls messageOnRide() with no arguments) and prevents straightforward implementation or compilation if students follow the problem/template while referencing the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Either: (A) Change the solution to match the problem/template by updating Rideable to declare String messageOnRide() (no parameters) and modify Pig and Seal to implement a no-arg messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", or (B) Update the problem statement and template examples to require messageOnRide(int speed) and adjust the described return string and example usages accordingly. Option A is recommended to preserve the current task description and template usage.

issues.description: The Rideable.messageOnRide method is specified in the problem statement (and expected by the template Main code) as a no-argument method returning a String (messageOnRide():String). In the solution repository, Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) introduces an int parameter and all implementing classes (Pig, Seal) implement the parameterized signature and produce messages including a speed. This creates a cross-artifact mismatch: students reading the problem and using the template will expect to call messageOnRide() with no arguments, but the solution API requires an int argument and returns a differently structured message. This inconsistency in the method signature and expected output is likely to confuse students mapping problem requirements to implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Rideable.messageOnRide method signature consistent across artifacts. Either remove the int parameter in the solution (change Rideable.messageOnRide(int speed) to messageOnRide()) and update Pig/Seal implementations to implement public String messageOnRide() returning "Riding on [Animal Type] [name]", or update the problem statement and template to require messageOnRide(int speed) and show expected output including the speed. Prefer aligning the solution to the problem/template by using the no-argument messageOnRide():String to minimize student confusion.
